item.title: UK Competition and Markets Authority in principle accepts remedies in AkzoNobel-Axalta merger
item.description: The UK’s Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) has confirmed that the remedy package offered on 18 November 2026 by Akzo Nobel N.V. and Axalta Coating Systems Ltd. could in principle address the CMA’s competition concerns raised on 11 November 2026 regarding the market for the supply of vehicle refinish (VR) coatings in the UK. The remedy package, which matches the package already agreed with the European Commission, involves the divestment of AkzoNobel’s European VR coatings business (including in the UK). AkzoNobel and Axalta will continue to work constructively with the CMA towards its final conditional clearance decision and remain confident that the merger will be completed by early 2027.

item.title: UPM, Ingredion, and Paramelt develop paper-based packaging structure
item.description: UPM Specialty Materials, Ingredion, and Paramelt have developed a prototype paper-based packaging structure that uses a starch-based barrier film to provide grease resistance. The prototype combines UPM’s Solide Lucent 78 gsm and UPM Asendo 65 gsm papers with a starch-based barrier coating from Ingredion and bio-based heat-seal and barrier coatings from Paramelt. Each company has contributed a different element of the structure, with the paper acting as the fibre-based substrate, the starch coating providing the grease barrier, and the heat-seal coating enabling the pack to be sealed. According to the companies involved, the prototype has passed Part 1 of Western Michigan University’s recyclability test.

item.title: Flint Group’s Flexocure® LEAP wins Sustainable Innovation category
item.description: Flint Group Packaging Solutions' Flexocure® LEAP won the Sustainable Innovation category at the 2026 BCF Awards. Judges were impressed by the UV Hg ink system’s 100% solids, VOC-free formulation, which helps printers avoid waste from solvent evaporation and ensure all applied ink remains on the substrate. Built using an entirely new resin technology, Flexocure® LEAP significantly reduces the risk of photoinitiator migration for indirect food contact packaging applications, while delivering the press performance expected of a high-quality UV flexographic ink for labels and flexible packaging.

item.title: International Paper names insider Nicholls CEO of DS Smith spinoff
item.description: Timothy Nicholls has been named as the CEO of DS Smith, the spinoff of packaging company International Paper. Nicholls is currently the executive vice president and president of International Paper's Europe, Middle East and Africa (EMEA) packaging business and previously served as the company's chief financial officer. DS Smith is expected to trade on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker "SMDS" around 7 December. It would also be listed for trading on the London Stock Exchange.

item.title: DS Smith's solutions awarded as best packaging for electronic devices in Spain
item.description: DS Smith, a company of International Paper and a leading global supplier of sustainable fibre-based packaging solutions, has been honoured with two awards at the 2026 edition of the Liderpack Awards, the national reference event for the packaging and POS sector organized by the Spanish Packaging Association and the Hispack trade fair. DS Smith’s ELapHug solution for protecting laptops in repair, and DS Smith Tecnicarton’s Ocean Transport Packaging for Electrical Cabinets, have shared the recognition as the best packaging of the year in the Electronics, Image and Sound category. Both projects share a common goal: to solve real customer challenges with solutions that drive efficiency, improve functionality and optimise material use. ELapHug is a corrugated cardboard solution specifically designed to protect laptops during transport to repair services. Its design allows a single packaging to be adapted to different laptop formats, integrating the fastening and separation elements, as well as a compartment for accessories.

item.title: Mondi presents an award-winning packaging concept that simplifies e-commerce packaging using laser marking
item.description: Mondi, a global leader in sustainable packaging and paper, has developed an award-winning packaging concept that combines a corrugated outer box with recyclable, laser-marked flexible packaging. This concept is designed for e-commerce and bag-in-box applications. It uses laser marking technology to apply designs directly onto the flexible packaging during the converting process, eliminating the need for conventional decorative printing and corresponding printing plates. This facilitates customisation, allows for quick design updates, and offers greater creative flexibility, helping customers respond more agilely to market trends and changing consumer preferences. The concept can be adapted to various flexible packaging formats, from reels to pre-formed pouches, such as the "re/cycle StripPouch" or larger pre-formed bags like the "re/cycle FlexiBag", promoting design for recycling by simplifying material structures and reducing decorative elements. Depending on application requirements, bio-based raw materials or post-consumer recycled content can be incorporated. Results from Mondi's internal product impact assessment indicate a significant reduction in CO2 emissions for the bio-based, laser-marked "StripPouch" compared to a conventional stand-up pouch, made from fossil fuels, printed, and laminated. This concept allows customers to benefit from shorter lead times, greater supply chain agility, and increased flexibility when introducing new products or designs. The concept won the German Packaging Award 2026 in the Sustainability category.

item.title: Survey reveals growing consumer trust in recycling
item.description: Pro Carton's 2026 European Consumer Packaging Perceptions Survey reveals that nearly six in ten Europeans are recycling more, while 84% say they prefer cartonboard packaging over plastic. Paper and cartonboard have achieved their highest-ever consumer trust levels for recycling, with 87% expressing confidence in their recyclability. This growing trust reflects the important role that established collection and recycling systems play in making circularity work in practice. Consumers are also demonstrating that sustainability influences purchasing decisions, with the research finding that 85% consider climate change at least sometimes when buying packaged goods, while 40% have bought more environmentally friendly products, an increase of nine percentage points compared with 2025.

item.title: AF&PA CEO issues statement on USTR findings in Section 301 investigation
item.description: Heidi Brock, President and CEO of the American Forest & Paper Association (AF&PA), has issued a statement on USTR's findings in the Section 301 investigation into structural excess capacity. Brock noted that non-market practices, particularly in China, are distorting global markets for pulp, paper, packaging, and tissue products. Chinese producers have added roughly 25 million tons of containerboard capacity since 2019, even as operating rates stay below 70%. Chinese paper exports rose more than 20% in some grades in 2025. Such exports displace American production and put at risk mills that support jobs in communities across the US. This excess capacity affects the domestic market in the US and works against the Administration's goal of strengthening US manufacturing.

item.title: The Penny Ice Creamery uses Solus DBX biobased coating
item.description: The Penny Ice Creamery is serving ice cream in paper cups coated with Eastman’s Solus DBX at all its locations. The Santa Cruz, California-based operator is the first to deploy the coating commercially to US consumers. Solus DBX is a biobased coating for paper food-service packaging. Certain formulations contain up to 93% biobased content. It is designed as an alternative to LDPE and PLA liners and can support industrial composting or paper recycling for some coated articles, depending on product design and local infrastructure.

item.title: Felix Schoeller files patent for multilayer paper-based packaging material
item.description: Germany-based Felix Schoeller GmbH & Co. has filed a patent for a multilayer paper-based packaging material designed for deep-drawing, the process used to form flat sheets into three-dimensional containers such as pots or trays. The proposed material consists of at least two paper layers joined by a polymer layer containing a water-soluble thermoplastic. This central layer acts as an adhesive, bonding the paper sheets together, while also supplying the flexibility needed for the material to be shaped during the deep-drawing process. The patent suggests the finished packaging could be more readily recycled through existing systems, as the polymer layer would dissolve during repulping rather than remaining as a persistent plastic component. The patent also outlines a production method for the material, in which the polymer is applied to one paper layer before this is joined to a second paper layer, forming the bonded structure described in the filing. The material is suitable for general packaging applications, with food packaging specifically mentioned as a potential use.

item.title: ProAmpac Introduces ProActive Intelligence Shelf Protect
item.description: ProAmpac, a global leader in flexible packaging and material science, has introduced the ProActive Intelligence™ Shelf Protect (SP) Series, designed for select meat, seafood, and dairy applications. The technology is FDA- and USDA-compliant for intended uses in fresh beef, fresh pork, cooked sausage, deli meat, fresh salmon, and fresh cheese. This direct food-contact biotechnology packaging helps reduce microbial growth associated with food spoilage in intended applications, supporting longer shelf life throughout storage and distribution. Shelf Protect maintains package clarity without altering the film's physical and seal properties and requires no on-package labeling for approved applications other than a "use by" or "use or freeze by" date.

item.title: Over 20 groups amend lawsuit to challenge California’s SB 54 EPR
item.description: The Flexible Packaging Association, the American Forest & Paper Association, and the Consumer Brands Association are among over 20 national and regional groups that amended an existing lawsuit to challenge California’s SB 54, the state’s EPR for packaging law. The case was filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of California. The lawsuit alleges that SB 54 uses the same broad definition of “recyclable” as SB 343, and does not adequately define “nonrecyclable” or “less likely to be recycled” in regards to source reduction. It also does not establish a clear compliance standard. Defendants include California Attorney General Rob Bonta, CalRecycle Director Zoe Heller, and Director of the Department of Tax and Fee Administration Trista Woessner-Gonzalez.

item.title: European Chemicals Agency's committees back PFAS restriction
item.description: The European Chemicals Agency's (ECHA) scientific committees have considered the current rules to be insufficient to control the emissions and risks of PFAS. These substances are used in many industries for their non-stick, waterproofing and stain-resistant properties, but their contamination is extraordinarily persistent. The Committee for Socio-economic Analysis supports a ban with justified exceptions for certain uses, with periods to develop alternatives. Each exemption will have to be demonstrated to be necessary, and the permitted uses will have to reduce their emissions, but this is not yet a comprehensive ban. The agency will send the opinions to the European Commission before the end of the year, after which the Commission will propose the restriction and EU countries will have to vote on it.

item.title: 16 new specifications for non-plastic packaging on the way for new PPWR requirements
item.description: The European Committee for Standardization (CEN) is working on 16 technical specifications for the design for recycling of packaging in materials other than plastic. According to the Swedish Institute for Standards (SIS), 16 new technical specifications for these packaging materials may be published in early 2027. Jenny Fagerland and Susanna Björk, both project managers at SIS, mentioned that one final vote remains. The hope is that the new documents can be published in early 2027.

item.title: AWA announces winners of 2026 International Sleeve Label Awards
item.description: Alexander Watson Associates (AWA) has announced the winners of the 2026 International Sleeve Label Awards. Ovelar won the Best in Show award for Señorío de Camarasa. In the TD Shrink category, CCL Label won for Sahara Dubai Chocolate Liqueur and IPE Indústria Gràfica S.L.U won for The Gabriel Boutet Champagne. Ovelar also won the Environmental Award for Sourz, which uses 40 percent post-consumer recycled PET and carries perforations with a clear call to action. Taurus Packaging Pvt Ltd received the Environmental Contribution honorable mention for Colgate Palmolive's Colgate Max Fresh. Steinhauser, Inc. won the Can Category for Vacali Sparkling Vodka.

item.title: Ball Corporation to set up beverage can manufacturing facility in Meerut
item.description: Ball Corporation, a US-based aluminium packaging manufacturer, is investing approximately USD 300 million to establish a two-line beverage can manufacturing facility in Meerut, Uttar Pradesh, India. The facility, located at the Integrated Manufacturing and Logistics Cluster (IMLC) in Meerut, is expected to commence operations in 2029. This will be Ball's third manufacturing facility in India, expanding its capacity to meet growing demand. The expansion comes as beverage cans remain a relatively small part of India's packaged drinks market, accounting for about 3% of sales. Demand for aluminium beverage cans in the country is estimated to nearly double by 2030.

item.title: Ardagh Metal Packaging plans new production line at Wrexham plant
item.description: Ardagh Metal Packaging (AMP) is looking to add a fifth production line at its beverage can plant in Wrexham, north Wales, which could create up to 60 new jobs. AMP is also looking to upgrade the processing speed of the plant's four existing lines. Apprenticeship roles would be created as well as the 60 jobs. The plant, on Wrexham Industrial Estate, produces about seven million drinks cans a day, with ends supplied from AMP's nearby site at Deeside.

item.title: MPMA welcomes agreement to link EU and UK ETS
item.description: The Metal Packaging Manufacturers Association (MPMA) has welcomed the agreement to link the UK and EU Emissions Trading Systems (ETS), saying it will help reduce costs and paperwork for manufacturers trading between the two markets. MPMA director and chief executive Jason Galley said removing CBAM charges between the UK and EU, along with the related requirements for emissions monitoring, reporting and verification, would reduce costs and administrative work for businesses. The MPMA also welcomed the UK government's plan to exempt goods originating in the EU, European Economic Area (EEA) and Switzerland from the UK CBAM from 1 January 2027. The EU's exemption is expected to take effect a year later, on 1 January 2028.

item.title: Fipec warns against anti-dumping duties on TiO₂
item.description: Fipec has warned that maintaining or strengthening anti-dumping duties on Chinese titanium dioxide (TiO₂) will increase the cost of an essential raw material and weaken the industries that use it. TiO₂, a white pigment with crucial functional properties, is essential for many formulations of paints, coatings, and inks. It is also used in plastics and paper manufacturing. To date, no substitute can achieve equivalent performance at a comparable cost and scale. For some formulations, TiO₂ represents up to 40% of the cost of raw materials and 20% of the cost of the finished product. In a sluggish market, marked by squeezed margins, the increased cost of this pigment directly impacts the competitiveness of European manufacturers and their customers, right up to the prices for the final consumer. Since the entry into force of the duties, several European TiO₂ production capacities have been shut down or are permanently unavailable. The European supply deficit is estimated at 327,000 tons per year, or around one-third of industrial demand.
